about: Dark tracks (dungeon/growth.py, requirements "Progression"): each grants power as it rises, rolls a lasting change at each threshold (filtered by the intensity settings), and at its top costs the player the character. `ask` is what the Continuity model is asked to look for.

corruption.name: Corruption
corruption.ask: made a pact or bargain with a fiend or anything under the Heartwood, used forbidden or fiendish power, or fed something that should not be fed
corruption.lost: The character is lost to what they bargained with. What walks on in their skin is not them, and the story ends for them here.

changes.text: Their shadow lags a moment behind them, and dogs will not come near.
Their eyes have gone black from lid to lid in poor light.
A brand like a closed hand has risen on their chest, warm to the touch, and it moves when they sleep.
They hear a patient voice when they are alone, and it is often right.
They no longer feel pity. They remember what it was, and can act it.
Priests and the devout know them on sight, and will not shelter them.
The Mammon faithful know them for one of their own and greet them as kin.
Fresh wounds on them close black and stinking, and something under the skin knits them.

addiction.name: Addiction
addiction.ask: took dust, dreamleaf, hard liquor to excess, or any drug
addiction.lost: The habit has the character now. They sell what they have and then themselves, and the story ends for them in a gutter on the Cyrel road.

changes.text: Their hands shake until they have had some.
Their teeth are going grey and loose.
Without it they cannot sleep more than an hour at a time.
They lie about it easily now, even to themselves.
Dealers greet them by name, and honest traders count their change twice.
They owe money to people who break fingers.

infamy.name: Infamy
infamy.ask: did something cruel, murderous or monstrous where others saw or will hear of it
infamy.lost: There is a price on the character's head in every town on the map, and someone has collected it. The story ends for them on a gibbet.

changes.text: Children are hushed when they pass, and shopkeepers serve them first to see them gone.
The watch has a drawing of their face, not a good one, but good enough.
Hard men come looking to make their names by killing them.
They have stopped flinching at blood, their own included.
A ballad about them goes round the taverns. It gets the worst of it right.
Someone tried to blind them for what they did, and nearly did.
